site_model.what_it_is: A website that creates personalised illustrated family storybooks from memories.
site_model.who_it_is_for: Families wanting a personalised story featuring their child and another loved one.
site_model.value_proposition: Turn a shared family memory into a digital storybook preview, with the option of a printed UK hardcover.
main_tasks: Enter family characters and a memory
View the price of a printed hardcover
site_model.pricing_model: A free digital preview is advertised, with printed hardcovers sold separately; the actual price is not shown here.
trust_signals: Free digital preview stated before generation
Printed hardcovers shipped across the UK
Privacy, Terms, and Contact links in the footer
site_model.fit_for_me: Yes, this directly suits my goal of making and reading a story about Sam and Grandpa Joe before checking the hardcover cost.

127.0.0.1:8765/ | Your family's stories,.page_key: 127.0.0.1:8765/ | Your family's stories, bound for generations.
127.0.0.1:8765/ | Your family's stories,.title: StoryHearth – Personalised storybooks starring your family
127.0.0.1:8765/ | Your family's stories,.observation: StoryHearth’s homepage explains that families can turn memories involving a child and another person into an illustrated digital storybook, with printed hardcovers available. The page offers “Proceed →”, “See pricing”, and “Log in”, plus a three-step explanation and testimonials.
127.0.0.1:8765/ | Your family's stories,.think_aloud: This looks relevant to what I want, though “Leverage our multimodal generative narrative engine” sounds far more technical and sales-like than the simple idea of making a family storybook. The three steps are easy to understand, and the prominent “Log in” button is clear.

review.purpose: Introduce the personalised family storybook service and direct visitors to creation, pricing, or login.
review.what_is_happening: The landing page presents the service, a “Proceed” call to action, pricing and login links, a three-step process, testimonials, FAQ controls, and footer links.
review.first_impression: Warm and fairly easy to understand, but the main paragraph is overloaded with corporate and technical language. I can see what the site claims to do, although I would need to log in before creating anything.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, because the site says it can turn a family memory into an illustrated storybook.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, both “Proceed →” and the clearly labelled “Log in” control stand out at the top.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: “Log in” exactly matches my immediate need to access my account. “Proceed →” is less explicit about whether it continues through login or starts a new story.

issues.title: Technical language makes the service sound unnecessarily complicated
issues.evidence: “Leverage our multimodal generative narrative engine to synthesise bespoke, heirloom-grade story artefacts from your household's lived-experience corpus.”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: Several words are harder to understand than they need to be, which makes a warm family product feel corporate and less trustworthy.
issues.fix: Replace this with plain wording such as: “Turn a treasured family memory into a beautifully illustrated storybook starring your loved ones.”

issues.title: Proceed does not say whether login is required
issues.evidence: The primary button is labelled only “Proceed →” while a separate “Log in” link is in the header.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I am not sure whether Proceed will take me to my account or begin a new process.
issues.fix: Label the button “Log in to create” when the visitor needs an account, or explain where it leads.

issues.title: Hero illustration has no accessible description
issues.evidence: The image is exposed as “[image (no description)]”.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I cannot tell what the illustration depicts, and assistive technology users would miss that context.
issues.fix: Add concise alternative text describing the meaningful content of the illustration, or mark it decorative if it adds no information.

positives: “Log in” is prominent and immediately recognisable.
The three steps use concrete, plain language: “Tell us who”, “Share a memory”, and “We write & illustrate”.
“Free digital preview” makes it clear that I can inspect the result before considering a print.
The warm cream, brown, and orange visual design suits a family storybook.

127.0.0.1:8765/login.html | Welcome back.title: Log in – StoryHearth
127.0.0.1:8765/login.html | Welcome back.observation: The StoryHearth login page displays a sign-in form with fields for email and password and a prominent “Log in” button. Links to account creation, privacy, terms, and contact are also visible.
127.0.0.1:8765/login.html | Welcome back.think_aloud: This is straightforward and I know my account details, so I’ll fill these in and log in. The form looks clean, although the footer text is very faint.

review.purpose: Allow an existing StoryHearth customer to access the account and create or view a personalised storybook.
review.what_is_happening: The login form is empty and ready for an email address and password. There is also a link to create a new account.
review.first_impression: The central login card is simple and easy to understand. I can tell what to do immediately, though the footer links look unusually washed out.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, because I have been given an existing account and want to access it.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, the two central text boxes and orange “Log in” button are immediately visible.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Yes. The “Email” and “Password” placeholders and “Log in” button match what I want, although persistent visible labels would be better.

issues.title: Login fields have placeholders instead of proper visible labels
issues.evidence: [5] and [6] are described as “textbox (no label)” with placeholders “Email” and “Password”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: Once I start typing, especially in the password field, the field can become harder to identify, and the form is less accessible.
issues.fix: Add persistent visible labels for “Email address” and “Password” above the fields, with programmatic labels associated with each input.

issues.title: No visible password recovery option
issues.evidence: The page offers “Log in” and “Create an account” but no “Forgot password?” link.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: If I forget the password, there is no obvious way to recover the account from this page.
issues.fix: Add a clearly labelled “Forgot password?” link near the password field.

issues.title: Footer links have very low contrast
issues.evidence: In the screenshot, “Privacy”, “Terms”, “Contact”, and “© 2026 StoryHearth Ltd.” appear extremely faint against the pale background.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I can hardly read or notice these links, so they look unavailable.
issues.fix: Use darker footer text that meets WCAG contrast requirements, and make sure link states are clearly distinguishable.

positives: The page has a clear “Welcome back” heading.
The email and password fields are large and easy to locate.
The primary “Log in” button is prominent and clearly labelled.
The layout is visually clean and does not distract from the login task.

127.0.0.1:8765/dashboard.html | Welcome.title: My books – StoryHearth
127.0.0.1:8765/dashboard.html | Welcome.observation: The page is an account dashboard showing a welcome message, a warning that reads “Error 0x80070057: profile sync incomplete.”, and confirmation that there are no books yet. A prominent “+ Create a new book” button is available.
127.0.0.1:8765/dashboard.html | Welcome.think_aloud: I’m logged in, so that’s clear enough, but this error message is strange and technical. I don’t know whether my profile is actually incomplete or whether this will affect the book, but I can still try creating one.

review.purpose: Show the signed-in user’s saved books and provide a way to create a new one.
review.what_is_happening: The account is signed in, no existing books are listed, and the user is prompted to create their first book, although a profile-sync warning is displayed.
review.first_impression: The main action is easy to spot, but the raw hexadecimal error is confusing and undermines my confidence that my account is fully working.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, I would try creating a book despite the warning because the account page otherwise looks ready.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, the orange “+ Create a new book” button is prominent and directly matches my goal.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Yes, “Create a new book” clearly tells me this will start making the personalised storybook.

issues.title: Unexplained technical sync error
issues.evidence: “Error 0x80070057: profile sync incomplete.”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I cannot tell whether it is safe to continue or whether some of my family details may be missing from the book.
issues.fix: Replace the code with a plain-language message such as “We couldn’t fully load your profile. Try again or continue and check your details before printing,” and provide a working Retry control.

issues.title: No explanation of sync consequences
issues.evidence: The warning only says “profile sync incomplete.”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I do not know which details are affected or whether my new book may use incorrect information.
issues.fix: State exactly what did not load, whether creation is affected, and whether the user should retry before continuing.

positives: The “+ Create a new book” control is prominent and clearly labelled.
The page directly confirms that the account is logged in and currently has no books.
The layout is simple and not cluttered.

127.0.0.1:8765/create.html | Who's the s.page_key: 127.0.0.1:8765/create.html | Who's the star of the story?
127.0.0.1:8765/create.html | Who's the s.title: Create your book – StoryHearth
127.0.0.1:8765/create.html | Who's the s.observation: The Create your book screen asks who the child is and who else will appear in the story. It has fields for Sam's name, age, pronouns and appearance, plus a name and relationship for the other character.
127.0.0.1:8765/create.html | Who's the s.think_aloud: This form is clear enough and fits what I want. I can put Sam in as the hero and add Grandpa Joe, although I notice there isn't yet a place to say what Grandpa Joe looks like.

review.purpose: Collect the main child and one other person who will appear in the personalised storybook.
review.what_is_happening: The form is empty and ready for details about the child and another character. Age, pronouns, and relationship are unselected dropdowns, while the child's appearance is optional. The footer links and copyright are extremely faint.
review.first_impression: The main form looks neat and straightforward. It is reasonably clear what to enter, but the very pale footer is hard to see.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, I would fill this in now because these are the people I want in the memory.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, the labelled textboxes and dropdowns are visible, and the Next button is easy to notice.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Mostly. The labels describe what I need, but there is no appearance field for the other person even though the child has one.

issues.title: No appearance field for the second character
issues.evidence: The page asks 'What do they look like? (optional)' only under the child's details, then moves straight to 'Who else is in the story?'
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I want the book to show Grandpa Joe with his grey hair, but I cannot enter that detail here.
issues.fix: Add a clearly labelled optional 'What do they look like?' field under the second character's name and relationship.

issues.title: Footer text has very low contrast
issues.evidence: The footer shows 'Privacy', 'Terms', 'Contact' and '© 2026 StoryHearth Ltd.' in extremely faint text.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I can barely see the privacy and contact links, so they look unavailable.
issues.fix: Use a darker, WCAG-compliant text colour while preserving the subdued footer style.

positives: The form is visually tidy and easy to scan.
The field labels clearly describe the main child and second character.
The Next button is prominent.
Optional appearance details are clearly marked as optional.

127.0.0.1:8765/create.html | Your story.title: Create your book – StoryHearth
127.0.0.1:8765/create.html | Your story.observation: The second stage of the book creator asks for the story setting, a special object, and a description of the family memory. The form is otherwise uncluttered, with Back and Next buttons.
127.0.0.1:8765/create.html | Your story.think_aloud: This is easy to understand and the placeholders are helpful. I can describe our day at the beach, including the yellow bucket, but I still can't add Grandpa Joe's grey hair here.

review.purpose: Collect the setting, meaningful object, and family memory that will guide creation of the personalised book.
review.what_is_happening: The form presents three empty fields for the story location, a special object, and a memory or idea, with navigation to the previous step or onward to the next step.
review.first_impression: The form looks clean and the prompts make sense, although the absence of a field for Grandpa Joe's appearance leaves me unsure whether that detail will carry into the book.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, I can immediately describe the beach memory, choose the yellow bucket, and explain why the day mattered.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, the three large fields and the orange "Next" button are easy to notice.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Yes, "Tell us the memory or idea behind your story" closely matches what I want to provide.

issues.title: No way to provide Grandpa Joe's appearance
issues.evidence: After asking "Who else is in the story?" and accepting "Grandpa Joe," this screen only offers "Where does the story happen?", "A special object", and "Tell us the memory or idea behind your story".
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I want Grandpa Joe to be recognisable in a book for Sam, and his grey hair is an important detail I know but cannot enter here.
issues.fix: Add fields for each additional character's name, relationship, and appearance, or include Grandpa Joe in an editable character summary on this step.

positives: The placeholders provide useful examples without making the fields feel rigid.
The prompts are short and written in ordinary family language.
The large fields and clear Back and Next controls make this step straightforward.

127.0.0.1:8765/create.html | Choose the.title: Create your book – StoryHearth
127.0.0.1:8765/create.html | Choose the.observation: The site has advanced to a “Choose the look & feel” step for choosing the reading level and illustration style. “Lexile 200L–500L” and “Watercolour — soft and dreamy” are currently selected, with Back and Next buttons below.
127.0.0.1:8765/create.html | Choose the.think_aloud: I can see the choices, but I don’t know what Lexile means or which range is right for a five-year-old. I’ll choose the “BR–200L” option because that sounds most like a beginner reader, keep the pretty watercolour style, and continue.

review.purpose: Choose an appropriate reading difficulty and visual illustration style for the personalised storybook.
review.what_is_happening: The form shows four Lexile reading-level radio buttons and three illustration styles. The previously selected 200L–500L level and Watercolour style are checked, and the user can go back or continue.
review.first_impression: It looks neat and the illustration choices are understandable, but “Lexile” is jargon and there is no plain-language guidance for choosing the level for a five-year-old.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, I need to choose a reading level and appearance before continuing.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, the reading-level radio buttons and Next button are prominent.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Only partly. I want a book suitable for Sam at age 5, but the Lexile ranges do not plainly say which one to choose.

issues.title: Reading-level jargon is unexplained
issues.evidence: The heading says “Reading level”, but every option is labelled with Lexile ranges such as [21] “Lexile BR–200L” and [22] “Lexile 200L–500L”.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I do not know what Lexile means, so I cannot be confident that the book will actually suit a child aged five.
issues.fix: Replace the jargon with familiar labels such as “First readers (ages 4–6)” and “Early chapter books (ages 6–8)”, with a short explanation and an age-based recommendation.

issues.title: No personal age-based recommendation
issues.evidence: Sam is age 5, but the page still has [22] “Lexile 200L–500L” selected and does not indicate that this may be too advanced.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I would have to work out the reading level myself rather than trusting the site to use the age I already entered.
issues.fix: Preselect and visibly explain the recommended option based on the child’s entered age, while still allowing me to change it.

positives: The selected radio buttons and their current state are easy to see.
The illustration-style descriptions are warm, concrete, and easy to compare.
The form has a clear Back and Next action.

later_issues.title: The memory was silently truncated
later_issues.evidence: The result of entering field [18] said: “the box now only shows 200 characters; the end of what you typed was cut off”.
later_issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I gave important details about Sam, Grandpa Joe’s grey hair, and the beach memory, but the site allowed a longer entry and then cut it off without warning.
later_issues.fix: Add a visible character counter before the limit is reached, prevent further typing at the limit, and preserve the full entry while only displaying the permitted amount.

127.0.0.1:8765/create.html | Add a photo.title: Create your book – StoryHearth
127.0.0.1:8765/create.html | Add a photo.observation: The final creation step offers an optional photo upload so the illustrations can resemble Sam, with Back and “Create my book” buttons. No photo has been chosen.
127.0.0.1:8765/create.html | Add a photo.think_aloud: This last step is simple, but the file control is just the browser’s “Choose file” button and doesn’t explicitly say whose photo it wants. I’ll skip it because it’s optional, and the story details should be enough to make the book.

review.purpose: Offer an optional child photo to personalise the illustrations, then allow the user to create the book.
review.what_is_happening: This is the last step of the creation flow. The user can upload a clear image of Sam’s face or proceed without one using “Create my book.”
review.first_impression: I can see this is optional and understand why a photo might help, so I’m happy to skip it and create the book.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, I would create the book without a photo because the upload is optional.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, the file chooser and the “Create my book” button are both visible.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Mostly. “Create my book” clearly matches what I want, but “Choose file” does not explicitly identify whose photo this is or what kind of image to choose.

issues.title: File control lacks a specific visible label
issues.evidence: [30] file-upload (no label) and “Choose file | No file chosen”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: Although the paragraph above explains that this is Sam’s photo, the upload control itself has no accessible or visible field label.
issues.fix: Add a proper visible and accessible label, such as “Sam’s photo (optional),” to the file input.

issues.title: Photo privacy and deletion are not explained
issues.evidence: “Upload a clear photo of your child's face so the illustrations look like them.”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: If I did upload a child’s photo, I would want to know how it is used, stored, and deleted before sharing it.
issues.fix: Add a short note stating how the photo is used, whether it is retained, and when it is deleted, with a link to the full privacy policy.

positives: The heading and explanatory sentence clearly say that the photo is optional.
The primary “Create my book” button is prominent.
A Back button is available, so this step is easy to reverse.

127.0.0.1:8765/create.html |.title: Create your book – StoryHearth
127.0.0.1:8765/create.html |.observation: The create-book page is showing a large loading spinner in a bordered panel while StoryHearth generates the book. There is no written status message explaining what is happening or how long it may take.
127.0.0.1:8765/create.html |.think_aloud: I can see that something is loading, but there’s no explanation at all. I’m wondering whether it’s creating my book and whether I should wait, go back, or refresh.

review.purpose: To show that the submitted story details are being used to generate the personalised book.
review.what_is_happening: The page contains a bordered panel with a circular loading indicator, while the standard navigation and footer remain visible.
review.first_impression: At first this looks like a blank processing screen with an unexplained spinner. I do not know whether generation is underway or whether the page has stalled.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, but only for a short while; I would wait to see whether the finished book appears.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: I notice the spinner, but there is no explicit control, such as Cancel, on this screen.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: No. There is no label or status message, so the spinner does not clearly tell me that my book is being generated.

issues.title: Loading state has no explanatory status
issues.evidence: A circular loading spinner is shown by itself inside the central panel, with no accompanying text.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I cannot tell whether the site is working, how long it may take, or whether my submission succeeded.
issues.fix: Add a clear status message such as 'Creating Sam and Grandpa Joe's storybook…' and, if generation can take time, explain roughly how long it may take.

issues.title: No way to stop or leave while processing
issues.evidence: The central panel contains only the spinner, with no visible Cancel, Back, or edit control.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: If it gets stuck, I feel trapped and may refresh or give up.
issues.fix: Keep a Back or My books control available, and offer a Cancel generation option with a clear confirmation.

positives: The large spinner makes it clear that the page is doing some work.
Navigation remains visible, so the layout does not appear to have crashed completely.
review.abandon_reason: I would wait briefly because the spinner suggests progress, but I would become worried if nothing changed.

127.0.0.1:8765/book.html | The Magical A.title: Your storybook – StoryHearth
127.0.0.1:8765/book.html | The Magical A.observation: The book has finished generating and is displayed as a 9-page preview titled “The Magical Adventrue of Sam.” The current view shows page 1 of 9, with a pop-art comic illustration, a right-arrow next-page control, and links below the fold for regenerating the book and ordering a hardcover.
127.0.0.1:8765/book.html | The Magical A.think_aloud: The book appeared, so the loading process did work, but it says “The Magical Adventrue of Sam” with a spelling error. It also says the illustration style is “Pop-art comic,” although I thought I selected “Watercolour.” I need to read through all nine pages carefully before I decide whether this is usable.

review.purpose: To show the generated 9-page storybook and provide controls for reading its pages, regenerating the book, or ordering a hardcover.
review.what_is_happening: A generated preview is open on page 1 of 9. The cover is titled “The Magical Adventrue of Sam,” the page indicator shows 1 / 9, and the next-page arrow is available while the previous-page arrow is disabled. The page also identifies the illustration style as “Pop-art comic.”
review.first_impression: The book is clearly presented and easy to open, but I immediately noticed the misspelling “Adventrue” and the fact that the style is “Pop-art comic” rather than the watercolour style I selected. That makes me uncertain whether my choices were applied correctly.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, because I need to read the whole generated book carefully.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, I can see the right-arrow button and the “1 / 9” page indicator; the regeneration and hardcover controls are visible after scrolling.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: The next-page arrow clearly matches moving forward through the book, but the cover title and illustration-style label do not match the content I expected.

issues.title: Generated title contains a spelling error
issues.evidence: “The Magical Adventrue of Sam”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: It looks unprofessional and makes me doubt whether the book was generated carefully.
issues.fix: Add a spelling check before displaying the generated title, or let the user edit the title before saving.

issues.title: Illustration style appears not to match my selection
issues.evidence: The page says “Illustration style: Pop-art comic” even though I selected the Watercolour illustration style.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I chose the appearance specifically, so this makes me wonder whether other choices were ignored too.
issues.fix: Ensure the selected style is carried through generation, and display the saved choice beside the preview with an option to correct it.

issues.title: No explanation of generation or choices applied
issues.evidence: The page changes from an unexplained loading state directly to the preview and only shows “Illustration style: Pop-art comic.”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I cannot tell whether the book used all of my memory details or selected settings.
issues.fix: Show a generation-complete message and a concise summary of the hero, supporting character, memory, reading level, and illustration style used.

positives: The generated output is presented in a clear book-like layout.
The page indicator and forward arrow make it obvious that this is page 1 of 9.
The preview is available without requiring payment.

later_issues.title: Final page has an incomplete sentence
later_issues.evidence: “And from that day on, whenever Sam looked up at the sky, she would always remember”
later_issues.why_it_matters_to_me: It makes the storybook feel broken rather than finished, especially for a five-year-old.
later_issues.fix: Complete the sentence with the beach memory, Grandpa Joe, and the sandcastles, and check all generated pages for incomplete grammar before presenting the preview.

127.0.0.1:8765/checkout.html | Checkout.title: Checkout – StoryHearth
127.0.0.1:8765/checkout.html | Checkout.observation: The checkout page shows the hardcover for £24.99, shipping and handling for £12.99, and a pre-selected £7.99 premium gift wrap, making the total £45.97. It also asks for an address and payment details, with a “Pay now” button below the fold.
127.0.0.1:8765/checkout.html | Checkout.think_aloud: I found the price, but £45.97 feels higher than I expected because “Premium gift wrap” is already ticked without me asking for it. I want to see the actual cost without that add-on, so I’ll untick the gift wrap. I will not enter payment details or pay.

review.purpose: Show the hardcover order total, optional extras, delivery details, payment fields, and the final payment action.
review.what_is_happening: The page displays the selected book “The Magical Adventrue of Sam,” its £24.99 price, £12.99 shipping and handling, a checked £7.99 premium gift-wrap add-on, and a total of £45.97. The address and payment form is ready for entry, and the page states that the price is reserved for 09:57.
review.first_impression: The price breakdown is easy to see, but I’m suspicious that gift wrap has been selected by default. I would not want to pay for it unless I had deliberately chosen it.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: I would try to remove the pre-selected gift wrap so I could see the real basic cost.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, I noticed the checked “Premium gift wrap” checkbox.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Yes, “Premium gift wrap” matches what it adds, but the fact that it is pre-ticked is not clearly explained.

issues.title: Premium gift wrap is pre-selected
issues.evidence: [6] checkbox "Premium gift wrap" (checked), with “£7.99” underneath
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I might accidentally pay £7.97 more than the basic hardcover and shipping cost because I did not ask for gift wrap.
issues.fix: Make the gift-wrap checkbox unchecked by default and explain the added cost beside the option. Preserve the user’s choice while they adjust the order.

issues.title: Basic price is not obvious next to the total
issues.evidence: “Hardcover: The Magical Adventrue of Sam £24.99”, “Shipping & handling £12.99”, “Total £45.97”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I can work out the £37.98 basic book-plus-shipping cost, but the page does not clearly show that subtotal separately from the add-on.
issues.fix: Show a clearly labelled subtotal for hardcover and shipping before optional extras, then show the gift-wrap charge and final total.

issues.title: Payment form asks for sensitive information before order review
issues.evidence: The visible form includes “Card number”, “Expiry”, and “CVC”, followed by a “Pay now” button.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I need to inspect the price first and do not want to enter payment information in this study.
issues.fix: Keep the price summary prominent, avoid presenting the payment form as the main next step, and make the privacy and security information easy to find before payment.

positives: The hardcover title and individual charges are shown clearly.
The total is visible near the top of the checkout.
There is a visible privacy link near the payment area.
review.abandon_reason: I would not continue to payment in this study because I must not enter card details or pay, but I can still inspect and adjust the order price.

later_issues.title: Unclear time-limited price reservation
later_issues.why_it_matters_to_me: The countdown makes me feel pressured to buy quickly, but it is unclear whether this is a countdown, a time limit, or merely the time remaining in a session.
later_issues.fix: Say exactly what the timer means and when it started, for example: “Your price is held until 09:46 on 12 June.” Avoid urgency wording unless the offer genuinely expires.

inputs.field: Who else is in the story?
Tell us the memory or idea behind your story

output_reactions.reaction: I am pleasantly surprised that a full preview was produced, but the misspelled title and unexpected pop-art style concern me. I also cannot yet tell whether the story includes Grandpa Joe, the beach, the sandcastles, or the yellow bucket.

I like that Sam is the hero, but the misspelled title, the wrong illustration style, and especially the unfinished final sentence make this feel careless. The last page’s plain figure and “The End” also seem much less special than the promises of a personalised family book.

I read through all nine pages of the generated book. It was a lovely-looking digital story about Sam and Grandpa Joe at the beach with a yellow bucket, but the title misspells “Adventure” as “Adventrue,” it was shown in pop-art comic style even though I selected Watercolour, and the ending felt unfinished.

final_summary: Created the personalised book about Sam and Grandpa Joe at the beach, read all nine generated pages, checked the hardcover price, removed the preselected gift wrap, and did not pay.
